meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'understand', paired with 'понять'.

examples.trans: Of course, I understand you perfectly.
I take it you have resumed your relationship?
I understand.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Без меня вы звезду не получите.
examples.trans: Without me you will never get a star.
Just do not get nervous right now.

examples.text: Скажите, вы на самом деле инвалид?
examples.trans: Tell me, are you really disabled?

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'зобновить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'resumed / renewed'.

examples.trans: I take it you have resumed your relationship?

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и возобновить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and resumed on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Thank you for your answer.
Your courage is worthy of great admiration.
Your business is postponed for a little while.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ношение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'relationship' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I take it you have resumed your relationship?

examples.text: А я испорчу отношения с будущим мэром.
examples.trans: And I'll ruin my relationship with the future mayor.
We have a very warm relationship.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Especially that evening on the roof.
Then we will see each other at home tonight.

examples.text: Я бы не стал этого делать.
examples.trans: I would not do that in your place.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Без меня вы звезду не получите.
examples.trans: Without me you will never get a star.

examples.text: На два часа я её уговорил.
examples.trans: I talked her into two hours a day.
A guest found a piece of metal in the soup.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will tell', paired with 'рассказывать'.

examples.text: Катюша, мне нужно кое-что тебе рассказать.
examples.trans: Katyusha, I need to tell you something.
Tell me what happened.
I'll tell Mum everything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No, she is not against it at all.
She is elderly, she could have mixed it up.
Perhaps it will seem strange to you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А Елена Павловна разве не против?
examples.trans: And is Elena Pavlovna not against it?
No, she is not against it at all.
They simply do not want to pay!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: He is their very chief inspector.
Because of an injury I had to leave the profession.
You recently came out of a coma.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'тому').

examples.text: Потому что мне очень надо идти.
examples.trans: Because I really need to go.
Because this is the pure truth.

examples.text: Потому что я люблю свою дочь.
examples.trans: Because I love my daughter.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Obviously, this is a clever con artist.
Wait, did he pay the money after all?

examples.text: Он подтвердил, что он отец Кости.
examples.trans: He confirmed that he is Kostya's father.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'like', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.text: Виктор не любит об этом говорить.
examples.trans: Viktor does not like to talk about this.
Look how much the child loves him.
I truly loved her very much.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Viktor decided to open his own restaurant.
He created his own signature menu.

examples.text: Хочу отразить это в своём отчёте.
examples.trans: I want to include this in my report.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning '(our) daughter' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А ну не трогай мою дочь!
examples.trans: Hey, do not touch my daughter!
For my daughter I will tear anyone apart!

examples.text: Потому что я люблю свою дочь.
examples.trans: Because I love my daughter.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Без меня вы звезду не получите.
examples.trans: Without me you will never get a star.

examples.text: На два часа я её уговорил.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will be'.

examples.trans: I just want to stay at home.
I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: From French 'chance' (favorable turn of the dice, from Late Latin 'cadentia').

examples.text: У неё будет шанс найти другого.
examples.trans: She will have a chance to find another man.
I've got every chance.
This is your chance.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: У неё будет шанс найти другого.
examples.trans: She will have a chance to find another man.
Where will I find movers?
I found the phone.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').

examples.text: Она вышла за моего лучшего друга.
examples.trans: She married my best friend.

examples.text: Вы выдавали себя за другого человека.
examples.trans: You passed yourself off as another person.
What do you mean, as another person?

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: For the test we need to take saliva.
And I read that hair is needed.
No, saliva is needed for the test.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Катюша, мне нужно кое-что тебе рассказать.
examples.trans: Katyusha, I need to tell you something.
And one more thing.
I want to show you something.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты же сама его недавно нашла.
examples.trans: You found him recently yourself, after all.
Yes, I get tired, there is a lot of work.
Yes, you tried very hard.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'mom' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Hello, Mom, hi, we are working.

examples.text: Мама, а ты что тут делаешь?
examples.trans: Mom, what are you doing here?
Mom, you will soon become a grandmother!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: He created his own signature menu.
Yes, this is my signature menu.

examples.text: Мы с тобой сколько инспекций прошли!
examples.trans: How many inspections you and I have been through!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will become', paired with 'становиться'.

examples.trans: She is elderly, she could have mixed it up.
No, better to let him stay at home.
For the test we need to take saliva.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'grandmother' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Бабушка сказала, это не отец Кости.
examples.trans: Grandmother said this is not Kostya's father.
I spoke with your grandmother.
Mom, you will soon become a grandmother!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А Елена Павловна разве не против?
examples.trans: And is Elena Pavlovna not against it?
No, she is not against it at all.

examples.text: На два часа я её уговорил.
examples.trans: I talked her into two hours a day.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dad' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That is simply a great idea, Dad!
Dad asked me to pick up test results.

examples.text: А у меня анализ папы Кости.
examples.trans: And I have Kostya's dad's test.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here, there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: He passed this along to you.
Here he is sitting before you.
Here is a small tender goose breast.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Just do not get nervous right now.
I only embellished everything slightly.

examples.text: У меня её только что украли.
examples.trans: Someone just stole it from me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'myself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Right now I will go sort it out myself.
He is their very chief inspector.

examples.text: Скажите, вы на самом деле инвалид?
examples.trans: Tell me, are you really disabled?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'знать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to recognise; to find out', paired with 'узнавать'.

examples.text: Она не узнала в вас отца Кости.
examples.trans: She did not recognize Kostya's father in you.

examples.text: Я вот только что сама узнала.
examples.trans: I just found out myself right now.
Did you recognise me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'our, ours', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: A guest found a piece of metal in the soup.

examples.text: Гость в супе из чечевицы нашёл.
examples.trans: The guest found it in the lentil soup.
But our chef does not give up.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Unfortunately, such is our life.

examples.text: Сегодня этот лжец спас вам жизнь.
examples.trans: Today this liar saved your life.
Our life is a small kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, this is just an ordinary bolt.
Tell me, who cooked this?
Obviously, this is a clever con artist.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('little').

examples.trans: Little children sense everything right away.
Here is a small tender goose breast.
Our life is a small kitchen.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: Yes, of course, come into the kitchen.
Our life is a small kitchen.
We're sitting in the kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А Елена Павловна разве не против?
examples.trans: And is Elena Pavlovna not against it?
No, she is not against it at all.

examples.text: На два часа я её уговорил.
examples.trans: I talked her into two hours a day.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are cooking', paired with 'приготовить'.

examples.trans: Tell me, who cooked this?
It does not matter who exactly cooked it.
That is why it was not he who cooked today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'частье'). Common neuter noun meaning 'happiness' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На ней мы готовим наше счастье.
examples.trans: In it we cook our happiness.
Happiness is getting closer, almost here!
I wish you great happiness!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'бирать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to choose, select, pick'.

examples.trans: We need to get out of here urgently.
We choose the needed ingredients ourselves.
He takes a long time choosing a new dish.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('needed').

examples.trans: For the test we need to take saliva.
And I read that hair is needed.
No, saliva is needed for the test.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'ingredients' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Right now you are our main ingredient.
We choose the needed ingredients ourselves.
There are only the freshest ingredients there.

meanings.en: to do, to get up to (something outrageous)
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'create', paired with 'сотворить'.

examples.trans: What are you doing over there right now?

examples.text: Если бы я тогда не притворился.
examples.trans: If I had not pretended back then.
Create and try something new!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Без меня вы звезду не получите.
examples.trans: Without me you will never get a star.

examples.text: А Елена Павловна разве не против?
examples.trans: And is Elena Pavlovna not against it?
No, she is not against it at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'бовать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to try; to taste', paired with 'попробовать'.

examples.trans: Have you tried investing it?
Taste the soup!

examples.text: Слушай, Аркаша, а ты не пробовал это вложить?
examples.trans: Listen, Arkasha, have you ever tried investing it?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Что-то я не хочу в кино.
examples.trans: Somehow I do not want to go to the movies.
Create and try something new!
Has something happened?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.trans: You are to blame for everything yourself!

examples.text: Я сегодня снова потерял своего отца.
examples.trans: Today I lost my father all over again.

examples.text: Это я во всём сама виновата.
examples.trans: I am to blame for everything myself.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is waiting for', paired with 'подождать'.

examples.trans: Don't wait for me.
I'm waiting for you.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big').

examples.trans: Your courage is worthy of great admiration.
Yes, I will come with great pleasure.
This swindler will demand a big ransom!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'града'). Common feminine noun meaning 'reward' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He deserved this reward.

examples.text: И тогда вас ждёт большая награда!
examples.trans: And then a great reward awaits you!

examples.text: То есть награды для меня не будет?
examples.trans: So there will be no reward for me, then?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'received', paired with 'получать'.

examples.text: Без меня вы звезду не получите.
examples.trans: Without me you will never get a star.

examples.text: Но его ресторан достоин получить звезду.
examples.trans: But his restaurant is worthy of receiving a star.
We received a Michelin star!

meanings.en: star (in the sky, hotel rating, or famous person)
meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'star' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Без меня вы звезду не получите.
examples.trans: Without me you will never get a star.
Which one of us needs the star?
The star is already almost ours!
